scope: TicketRepository.reserveTickets default method on the existing ordinary-ticket branch
semantic_summary_origin: human-audited decompiled body plus binary SQL annotations and unchanged replay witness; not an automatically proved compiler transformation

input.order: original ticketIds encounter order, including multiplicity
preserve: Java attendee selection and metadata serialization semantics

proposal: Specialize the fixed named-parameter batch into a typed database entry executing the same ordered UPDATE effects and returning the same aggregate update count. Retain Java-side value conversions until an ABI is verified.
preserved_context: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED selection and insufficient-stock guard before the region
row-count validation immediately after the region
all additional-field reads and writes after the region
original first-ticket read after additional-field processing
Java price/VAT/discount computation and subsequent price update
billing, audit, payment applicability, extension/event effects and commit/rollback
not_claimed: deletion of unused data or safety modules
admission_obligations: recover and check complete typed binding ABI, including nulls, metadata encoding and enum casts
preserve per-row order, duplicate-ID behavior and affected-row accounting; do not equate batch SUCCESS_NO_INFO with a row count
preserve service-visible exception class/SQLSTATE and rollback for statement failures; unresolved cases remain barriers
preserve invoker privileges, RLS and same-connection transaction scope; never use SECURITY DEFINER or autonomous commits
prove no hidden trigger/effect semantics are dropped and preserve relevant constraint/trigger ordering
dispatch to the old path before executing any new writes when eligibility is unknown; never retry the old path after partial new writes
compare complete results and all table states before measuring performance; accept a no-speedup result

rejected_expansion.idea: merge batch writes with the subsequent first-ticket read by moving the read earlier
rejected_expansion.reason: actual additional-field processing lies between them; empty fixture tables do not prove those calls lack required effects
